382.s:
agnir uvāca
āgneyaṃ brahmarūpante purāṇaṃ kathataṃ mayā /
saprapañcaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ vidyādvayamayaṃ mahat //
382.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
आग्नेयं ब्रह्मरूपन्ते पुराणं कथतं मया /
सप्रपञ्चं निष्प्रपञ्चं विद्याद्वयमयं महत् //
382.m: Agni said: / This Purāṇa of Agni, whose form is brahman, has been spoken to you by me, / both with the manifest world and beyond it, consisting of the two knowledges, great.

382.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvākhyā vidyā viṣṇurjagajjaniḥ /
chandaḥ śikṣā vyākaraṇaṃ nighaṇṭujyotirākhyakāḥ //
382.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामाथर्वाख्या विद्या विष्णुर्जगज्जनिः /
छन्दः शिक्षा व्याकरणं निघण्टुज्योतिराख्यकाः //
382.m: The knowledge known as the Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Atharva [Vedas] is Viṣṇu, the origin of the world; / [and] those known as metrics, phonetics, grammar, lexicon, astronomy,

382.s:
niruktadharmaśāstrādi mīmāṃsānyāyavistarāḥ /
āyurvedapurāṇākhyā dhanurgandharvavistarāḥ //
382.d:
निरुक्तधर्मशास्त्रादि मीमांसान्यायविस्तराः /
आयुर्वेदपुराणाख्या धनुर्गन्धर्वविस्तराः //
382.m: Etymology, the legal treatises and the like, the expositions of Mīmāṃsā and Nyāya, / the expositions known as medicine, the Purāṇas, archery, and music,

382.s:
vidyā saivārthaśāstrākhyā devāntānyā harirmahān /
ityeṣā cāparā vidyā parividyākṣaraṃ paraṃ //
382.d:
विद्या सैवार्थशास्त्राख्या देवान्तान्या हरिर्महान् /
इत्येषा चापरा विद्या परिविद्याक्षरं परं //
382.m: And that knowledge known as statecraft—the other, supreme Hari extends unto the gods. / This is the lower knowledge; the higher knowledge is the supreme, imperishable [brahman].

382.s:
yasya bhāvo 'khilaṃ viṣṇustasya no bādhate kaliḥ /
aniṣṭvā tu mahāyajñānakṛtvāpi pitṛsvadhāṃ //
382.d:
यस्य भावो ऽखिलं विष्णुस्तस्य नो बाधते कलिः /
अनिष्ट्वा तु महायज्ञानकृत्वापि पितृस्वधां //
382.m: He whose conviction is that all is Viṣṇu is not oppressed by the Kali age. / Even without having performed the great sacrifices, and without making the ancestral offerings,

382.s:
kṛṣṇamabhyarcayanbhaktyā nainaso bhājanaṃ bhavet /
sarvakāraṇamatyantaṃ viṣṇuṃ dhyāyanna sīdati //
382.d:
कृष्णमभ्यर्चयन्भक्त्या नैनसो भाजनं भवेत् /
सर्वकारणमत्यन्तं विष्णुं ध्यायन्न सीदति //
382.m: One who worships Kṛṣṇa with devotion does not become a receptacle of sin. / Meditating on Viṣṇu, the ultimate cause of all, he does not sink down.

382.s:
anyatantrādidoṣottho viṣayākṛṣṭamānasaḥ /
kṛtvāpi pāpaṃ govindaṃ dhyāyanpāpaiḥ pramucyate //
382.d:
अन्यतन्त्रादिदोषोत्थो विषयाकृष्टमानसः /
कृत्वापि पापं गोविन्दं ध्यायन्पापैः प्रमुच्यते //
382.m: A person whose mind is seduced by sense objects, born from the fault of other systems and the like, / even having committed sin, is freed from sins by meditating on Govinda.

382.s:
taddhyānaṃ yatra govindaḥ sa kathā yatra keśavaḥ /
tat karma yattadarthīyaṃ kimanyair bahubhāṣitaiḥ //
382.d:
तद्ध्यानं यत्र गोविन्दः स कथा यत्र केशवः /
तत् कर्म यत्तदर्थीयं किमन्यैर् बहुभाषितैः //
382.m: That is meditation wherein is Govinda; that is a tale wherein is Keśava; / that is action which is performed for his sake. What is the use of other extensive talk?

382.s:
na tat pitā tu putrāya na śiṣyāya gururdvija /
paramārthaṃ paraṃ brūyādyadetatte mayoditaṃ //
382.d:
न तत् पिता तु पुत्राय न शिष्याय गुरुर्द्विज /
परमार्थं परं ब्रूयाद्यदेतत्ते मयोदितं //
382.m: Neither a father to his son, nor a guru to his disciple, O twice-born, / would declare that supreme reality which has been proclaimed to you by me.

382.s:
saṃsāre bhramatā labhyaṃ putradāradhanaṃ vasu /
:p 355
suhṛdaś ca tathaivānye nopadeśo dvijedṛśaḥ //
382.d:
संसारे भ्रमता लभ्यं पुत्रदारधनं वसु /
:प् 355
सुहृदश् च तथैवान्ये नोपदेशो द्विजेदृशः //
382.m:
Sons, wives, riches, and property may be obtained by one wandering in saṃsāra,
[Page 355]
And likewise other friends; but such teaching as this is not [attained], O twice-born.

382.s:
kiṃ putradārair mitrair vā kiṃ mitrakṣetravāndhavaiḥ /
upadeśaḥ paro vandhurīdṛśo yo vimuktaye //
382.d:
किं पुत्रदारैर् मित्रैर् वा किं मित्रक्षेत्रवान्धवैः /
उपदेशः परो वन्धुरीदृशो यो विमुक्तये //
382.m: What is the use of sons, wives, or friends? What is the use of friends, lands, and relatives? / Such teaching as leads to liberation is the supreme kin.

382.s:
dvividho bhūtamārgīyaṃ daiva āsura eva ca /
viṣṇubhaktiparo daivo viparītas tathāsuraḥ //
382.d:
द्विविधो भूतमार्गीयं दैव आसुर एव च /
विष्णुभक्तिपरो दैवो विपरीतस् तथासुरः //
382.m: The path of living beings is twofold: divine and demonic. / The divine is devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu; the demonic is the opposite of that.

382.s:
etat pavitramārogyaṃ dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ /
sukhaprītikaraṃ nṝṇāṃ mokṣakṛdyattaveritaṃ //
382.d:
एतत् पवित्रमारोग्यं धन्यं दुःस्वप्ननाशनं /
सुखप्रीतिकरं नॄणां मोक्षकृद्यत्तवेरितं //
382.m: This which has been told to you is purifying, health-giving, auspicious, destroying bad dreams, / granting happiness and affection to men, and bringing about liberation.

382.s:
yeṣāṃ gṛheṣu likhitamāgneyaṃ hi purāṇakaṃ /
pustakaṃ sthāsyati sadā tatra neśurupadravāḥ //
382.d:
येषां गृहेषु लिखितमाग्नेयं हि पुराणकं /
पुस्तकं स्थास्यति सदा तत्र नेशुरुपद्रवाः //
382.m: In whosever homes this Purāṇa of Agni shall abide / as a written book, calamities can never rule there.

382.s:
kiṃ tīrthair gopradānair vā kiṃ yajñaiḥ kimupoṣitaiḥ /
āgneyaṃ ye hi śṛṇvanti ahanyahani mānavāḥ //
382.d:
किं तीर्थैर् गोप्रदानैर् वा किं यज्ञैः किमुपोषितैः /
आग्नेयं ये हि शृण्वन्ति अहन्यहनि मानवाः //
382.m: What need is there of sacred fords, or gifts of cows, or sacrifices, or fasts, / for those men who hear the Agni Purāṇa day after day?

382.s:
ye dadāti tilaprasthaṃ suvarṇasya ca māṣakaṃ /
śṛṇoti ślokamekañca āgneyasya tadāpnuyāt //
382.d:
ये ददाति तिलप्रस्थं सुवर्णस्य च माषकं /
शृणोति श्लोकमेकञ्च आग्नेयस्य तदाप्नुयात् //
382.m: Whoever gives a prastha of sesame and a māṣa of gold, / and hears even a single verse of the Agni Purāṇa, attains that [fruit].

382.s:
adhyāyapaṭhanañcāsya gopradānād viśiṣyate /
ahorātrakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śrotumicchoḥ praṇaśyati //
382.d:
अध्यायपठनञ्चास्य गोप्रदानाद् विशिष्यते /
अहोरात्रकृतं पापं श्रोतुमिच्छोः प्रणश्यति //
382.m: The recitation of a chapter of this excels the gift of a cow. / The sin committed day and night is destroyed for one who desires to hear it.

382.s:
kapilānāṃ śate datte yad bhavejjyeṣṭhapuṣkare /
tadāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ hi paṭhitvā phalamāpnuyāt //
382.d:
कपिलानां शते दत्ते यद् भवेज्ज्येष्ठपुष्करे /
तदाग्नेयं पुराणं हि पठित्वा फलमाप्नुयात् //
382.m: Whatever [fruit] there is when a hundred tawny cows are given at Jyeṣṭhapuṣkara, / he obtains that very fruit having read the Agni Purāṇa.

382.s:
pravṛttañca nivṛttañca dharmaṃ vidyādvayātmakaṃ /
āgneyasya purāṇasya śāstrasyāsya samaṃ na hi //
382.d:
प्रवृत्तञ्च निवृत्तञ्च धर्मं विद्याद्वयात्मकं /
आग्नेयस्य पुराणस्य शास्त्रस्यास्य समं न हि //
382.m: Regarding duty characterized by worldly engagement and cessation, consisting of the two knowledges, / there is indeed nothing equal to this treatise, the Agni Purāṇa.

382.s:
paṭhannāgneyakaṃ nityaṃ śṛṇvan vāpi purāṇakaṃ /
bhakto vaśiṣṭha manujaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
382.d:
पठन्नाग्नेयकं नित्यं शृण्वन् वापि पुराणकं /
भक्तो वशिष्ठ मनुजः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते //
382.m: Constantly reciting or hearing the Agni Purāṇa, / a devoted man, O Vasiṣṭha, is freed from all sins.

382.s:
nopasargā na cānarthā na caurāribhayaṃ gṛhe /
tasman syād yatra cāgneyapurāṇasya hi pustakaṃ //
:p 356
382.d:
नोपसर्गा न चानर्था न चौरारिभयं गृहे /
तस्मन् स्याद् यत्र चाग्नेयपुराणस्य हि पुस्तकं //
:प् 356
382.m:
There are no afflictions, no misfortunes, and no fear of thieves or enemies in the house / of that person where the book of the Agni Purāṇa is kept.
[Page 356]

382.s:
na garbhahāriṇībhītirna ca bālagrahā gṛhe /
yatrāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ syānna piśācādikaṃ bhayaṃ //
382.d:
न गर्भहारिणीभीतिर्न च बालग्रहा गृहे /
यत्राग्नेयं पुराणं स्यान्न पिशाचादिकं भयं //
382.m: There is no fear of child-snatching spirits, nor seizing spirits of children in the house / where the Agni Purāṇa is; there is no fear of piśācas and the like.

382.s:
śṛṇvanvipro vedavit syāt kṣatriyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
ṛddhiṃ prāpnoti vaiśyaś ca śūdraścārogyamṛcchati //
382.d:
शृण्वन्विप्रो वेदवित् स्यात् क्षत्रियः पृथिवीपतिः /
ऋद्धिं प्राप्नोति वैश्यश् च शूद्रश्चारोग्यमृच्छति //
382.m: Hearing it, a brahmin becomes a knower of the Veda; a kṣatriya, a ruler of the earth; / a vaiśya attains prosperity; and a śūdra attains freedom from illness.

382.s:
yaḥ paṭhetśṛṇuyānnityaṃ samadṛgviṣṇumānasaḥ /
brahmāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ sattatra naśyantyupadravāḥ //
382.d:
यः पठेत्शृणुयान्नित्यं समदृग्विष्णुमानसः /
ब्रह्माग्नेयं पुराणं सत्तत्र नश्यन्त्युपद्रवाः //
382.m: Whoever, with mind impartial and fixed on Viṣṇu, recites or hears daily / this true Purāṇa of Agni and Brahmā, in that place calamities perish,

382.s:
divyāntarīkṣabhaumādyā duḥsvapnādyabhicārakāḥ /
yaccānyadduritaṃ kiñcittatsarvaṃ hanti keśavaḥ //
382.d:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमाद्या दुःस्वप्नाद्यभिचारकाः /
यच्चान्यद्दुरितं किञ्चित्तत्सर्वं हन्ति केशवः //
382.m: Celestial, atmospheric, terrestrial, and the like, bad dreams, malevolent sorceries, / and whatever other misfortune there may be: Keśava destroys all that.

382.s:
paṭhataḥ śṛṇvataḥ puṃsaḥ pustakaṃ yajato mahat /
āgneyaṃ śrīpurāṇaṃ hi hemante yaḥ śṛṇoti vai //
382.d:
पठतः शृण्वतः पुंसः पुस्तकं यजतो महत् /
आग्नेयं श्रीपुराणं हि हेमन्ते यः शृणोति वै //
382.m: For the man who recites, hears, and worships this great book, / the auspicious Purāṇa of Agni—whoever hears it in early winter,

382.s:
prapūjya gandhapuṣpādhyair agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet /
śiśire puṇḍarīkasya vasante cāśvamedhajam //
382.d:
प्रपूज्य गन्धपुष्पाध्यैर् अग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् /
शिशिरे पुण्डरीकस्य वसन्ते चाश्वमेधजम् //
382.m: Having worshipped it with fragrances, flowers, and the like, obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice; / in late winter, [the fruit] of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice; and in spring, that born of an Aśvamedha;

382.s:
grīṣme tu vājapeyasya rājasūyasya varṣati /
gosahasrasya śaradi phalaṃ tatpaṭhato hy ṛtau //
382.d:
ग्रीष्मे तु वाजपेयस्य राजसूयस्य वर्षति /
गोसहस्रस्य शरदि फलं तत्पठतो ह्य् ऋतौ //
382.m: In summer, that of a Vājapeya; in the rainy season, that of a Rājasūya; / in autumn, the fruit of a thousand cows for one who reads it in that season.

382.s:
āgneyaṃ hi purāṇaṃ yo bhaktyāgre paṭhete hareḥ /
so 'rcayecca vasiṣṭheha jñānayajñena keśavam //
382.d:
आग्नेयं हि पुराणं यो भक्त्याग्रे पठेते हरेः /
सो ऽर्चयेच्च वसिष्ठेह ज्ञानयज्ञेन केशवम् //
382.m: Whoever recites the Agni Purāṇa with devotion before Hari, / he worships Keśava here, O Vasiṣṭha, with a sacrifice of knowledge.

382.s:
yasyāgneyapurāṇasya pustakaṃ tasya vai jayaḥ /
likhitaṃ pūjitaṃ gehe bhuktirmuktiḥ kare 'sti hi //
382.d:
यस्याग्नेयपुराणस्य पुस्तकं तस्य वै जयः /
लिखितं पूजितं गेहे भुक्तिर्मुक्तिः करे ऽस्ति हि //
382.m: He who has the book of the Agni Purāṇa indeed has victory; / when it is copied and worshipped in his house, worldly enjoyment and liberation are in his hand.

382.s:
iti kālāgnirūpeṇa gītaṃ me hariṇā purā /
āgneyaṃ hi purāṇaṃ vai brahmavidyādvayāspadam /
vidyādvayaṃ vasiṣṭhedaṃ bhaktebhyaḥ kathayiṣyasi //
382.d:
इति कालाग्निरूपेण गीतं मे हरिणा पुरा /
आग्नेयं हि पुराणं वै ब्रह्मविद्याद्वयास्पदम् /
विद्याद्वयं वसिष्ठेदं भक्तेभ्यः कथयिष्यसि //
382.m: Thus was sung to me formerly by Hari in the form of the Fire of Time, / the Agni Purāṇa, the abode of the two knowledges of brahman. / You shall declare these two knowledges, O Vasiṣṭha, to the devotees.

382.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
vyāsāgneyapurāṇaṃ te rūpaṃ vidyādvayātmakaṃ /
kathitaṃ brahmaṇo viṣṇoragninā kathitaṃ yathā //
:p 357
382.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
व्यासाग्नेयपुराणं ते रूपं विद्याद्वयात्मकं /
कथितं ब्रह्मणो विष्णोरग्निना कथितं यथा //
:प् 357
382.m:
Vasiṣṭha said: / O Vyāsa, the form of the Agni Purāṇa, consisting of the two knowledges / of the brahman that is Viṣṇu, has been spoken to you just as it was spoken by Agni.
[Page 357]

382.s:
sārdhaṃ devaiś ca munibhirmahyaṃ sarvāthadarśakaṃ /
purāṇamagninā gautamāgneyaṃ brahmasanmitaṃ //
382.d:
सार्धं देवैश् च मुनिभिर्मह्यं सर्वाथदर्शकं /
पुराणमग्निना गौतमाग्नेयं ब्रह्मसन्मितं //
382.m: Together with the gods and sages, the Purāṇa showing all aims was proclaimed to me / by Agni, equal to the true brahman, O descendant of Gotama.

382.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyāddhyāsa likhedvā lekhayedapi /
śrāvayetpāṭhayedvāpi pūjayeddhārayedapi //
382.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्ध्यास लिखेद्वा लेखयेदपि /
श्रावयेत्पाठयेद्वापि पूजयेद्धारयेदपि //
382.m: Whoever recites, hears, meditates on it, writes it or has it written, / causes it to be heard or causes it to be recited, worships it or keeps it,

382.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāprakāmo divaṃ vrajet /
lekhayitvā purāṇaṃ yo dadyādviprebhya uttamaṃ //
382.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्राप्रकामो दिवं व्रजेत् /
लेखयित्वा पुराणं यो दद्याद्विप्रेभ्य उत्तमं //
382.m: Freed from all sins, having attained his desires, goes to heaven. / Having had this excellent Purāṇa transcribed, whoever gives it to brahmins

382.s:
sa brahmalokamāpnoti kulānāṃ śatamuddharet /
ekaṃ ślokaṃ paṭhedyastu pāpapaṅkādvimucyate //
382.d:
स ब्रह्मलोकमाप्नोति कुलानां शतमुद्धरेत् /
एकं श्लोकं पठेद्यस्तु पापपङ्काद्विमुच्यते //
382.m: He attains the realm of Brahmā and redeems a hundred families. / And one who recites even a single verse is freed from the mire of sin.

382.s:
tasmādvyāsa sadā śrāvyaṃ śiṣyebhyaḥ sarvadarśanaṃ /
śukādyair munibhiḥ sardhaṃ śrotukāmaiḥ purāṇakaṃ //
382.d:
तस्माद्व्यास सदा श्राव्यं शिष्येभ्यः सर्वदर्शनं /
शुकाद्यैर् मुनिभिः सर्धं श्रोतुकामैः पुराणकं //
382.m: Therefore, O Vyāsa, this Purāṇa containing all viewpoints should always be recited to disciples / along with sages like Śuka and others who desire to hear it.

382.s:
āgneyaṃ paṭhitaṃ dhyātaṃ śubhaṃ syād bhuktimuktidaṃ /
agnaye tu namastasmai yena gītaṃ purānakaṃ //
382.d:
आग्नेयं पठितं ध्यातं शुभं स्याद् भुक्तिमुक्तिदं /
अग्नये तु नमस्तस्मै येन गीतं पुरानकं //
382.m: The Agni Purāṇa, when recited and meditated upon, brings auspiciousness and bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Reverence unto that Agni by whom this Purāṇa was sung!

382.s:
vyāsa uvāca
vasiṣṭhena purā gītaṃ sūtaitatte mayoditaṃ /
parāvidyāparāvidyāsvarūpaṃ paramaṃ padam //
382.d:
व्यास उवाच
वसिष्ठेन पुरा गीतं सूतैतत्ते मयोदितं /
पराविद्यापराविद्यास्वरूपं परमं पदम् //
382.m: Vyāsa said: / Formerly sung by Vasiṣṭha, this which is the highest state, / embodying higher knowledge and lower knowledge, has been told to you by me, O Sūta.

382.s:
āgneyaṃ durlabhaṃ rūpaṃ prāpyate bhāgyasaṃyutaiḥ /
dhyāyanto brahma cāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ harimāgatāḥ //
382.d:
आग्नेयं दुर्लभं रूपं प्राप्यते भाग्यसंयुतैः /
ध्यायन्तो ब्रह्म चाग्नेयं पुराणं हरिमागताः //
382.m: The form of the Agni Purāṇa, difficult to obtain, is acquired by the fortunate. / Meditating upon the Agni Purāṇa as Brahman, they have attained Hari.

382.s:
vidyārthinas tathā vidyāṃ rājyaṃ rājyārthino gatāḥ /
aputrāḥ putriṇaḥ santi nāśrayā āśrayaṃ gatāḥ //
382.d:
विद्यार्थिनस् तथा विद्यां राज्यं राज्यार्थिनो गताः /
अपुत्राः पुत्रिणः सन्ति नाश्रया आश्रयं गताः //
382.m: Those seeking knowledge attain knowledge; those seeking kingship attain kingship; / the childless become possessors of children; the shelterless attain shelter;

382.s:
saubhāgyārthī ca saubhāgyaṃ mokṣaṃ mokṣārthino gatāḥ /
likhanto lekhayantaś ca niṣpāpaś ca śriyaṃ gatāḥ //
382.d:
सौभाग्यार्थी च सौभाग्यं मोक्षं मोक्षार्थिनो गताः /
लिखन्तो लेखयन्तश् च निष्पापश् च श्रियं गताः //
382.m: the seeker of good fortune attains good fortune; those seeking liberation attain liberation. / Those who write it or cause it to be written, become sinless and attain prosperity.

382.s:
śukapailamukhaiḥ sūta āgneyantu purāṇakaṃ /
rūpaṃ cintaya yātāsi bhuktiṃ muktiṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
382.d:
शुकपैलमुखैः सूत आग्नेयन्तु पुराणकं /
रूपं चिन्तय यातासि भुक्तिं मुक्तिं न संशयः //
382.m: O Sūta, together with prominent sages like Śuka and Paila, / meditate upon the form of the Agni Purāṇa; you will attain worldly enjoyment and liberation, there is no doubt.

382.s:
śrāvaya tvañca śiṣyebhyo bhaktebhyaś ca purāṇakam /
:p 358
sūta uvāca
vyāsa prasādādāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ śrutamādarāt //
382.d:
श्रावय त्वञ्च शिष्येभ्यो भक्तेभ्यश् च पुराणकम् /
:प् 358
सूत उवाच
व्यास प्रसादादाग्नेयं पुराणं श्रुतमादरात् //
382.m:
And you, recite this Purāṇa to disciples and devotees.
[p. 358]
Sūta said: / By the grace of Vyāsa, the Agni Purāṇa has been heard with reverence.

382.s:
āgneyaṃ brahmarūpaṃ hi munayaḥ śaunakādayaḥ /
bhavanto naimiṣāraṇye yajanto harimīśvaraṃ //
382.d:
आग्नेयं ब्रह्मरूपं हि मुनयः शौनकादयः /
भवन्तो नैमिषारण्ये यजन्तो हरिमीश्वरं //
382.m: The Agni Purāṇa is indeed the very form of Brahman, O sages headed by Śaunaka! / You, abiding in the Naimiṣa forest, worshipping Hari the Lord,

382.s:
tiṣṭhantaḥ śraddhayā yuktāstasmādvaḥ samudīritam /
agninā proktamāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ vedasammitaṃ //
382.d:
तिष्ठन्तः श्रद्धया युक्तास्तस्माद्वः समुदीरितम् /
अग्निना प्रोक्तमाग्नेयं पुराणं वेदसम्मितं //
382.m: remaining endowed with faith—therefore it has been declared to you: / the Agni Purāṇa, spoken by Agni, equal to the Vedas,

382.s:
brahmavidyādvayopetaṃ bhuktidaṃ muktidaṃ mahat /
nāsmātparataraḥ sāro nāsmātparataraḥ suhṛt //
382.d:
ब्रह्मविद्याद्वयोपेतं भुक्तिदं मुक्तिदं महत् /
नास्मात्परतरः सारो नास्मात्परतरः सुहृत् //
382.m: accompanied by both kinds of knowledge of Brahman, bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation, great. / There is no essence higher than this; there is no friend higher than this.

382.s:
nāsmātparataro grantho nāsmātparataro gatiḥ /
nāsmātparataraṃ śāstraṃ nāsmātparatarā śrutiḥ //
382.d:
नास्मात्परतरो ग्रन्थो नास्मात्परतरो गतिः /
नास्मात्परतरं शास्त्रं नास्मात्परतरा श्रुतिः //
382.m: There is no text higher than this; there is no refuge higher than this. / There is no treatise higher than this; there is no revealed scripture higher than this.

382.s:
nāsmātparataraṃ jñānaṃ nāsmātparatarā smṛtiḥ /
nāsmātparo hy āgamo 'sti nāsmādvidyā parāsti hi //
382.d:
नास्मात्परतरं ज्ञानं नास्मात्परतरा स्मृतिः /
नास्मात्परो ह्य् आगमो ऽस्ति नास्माद्विद्या परास्ति हि //
382.m: There is no knowledge higher than this; there is no remembered tradition higher than this. / There is indeed no Āgama higher than this, nor is there any higher knowledge than this.

382.s:
nāsmātparaḥ syātsiddhanto nāsmātparamamaṅgalam /
nāsmātparo 'sti vedāntaḥ purāṇaṃ paramantvidaṃ //
382.d:
नास्मात्परः स्यात्सिद्धन्तो नास्मात्परममङ्गलम् /
नास्मात्परो ऽस्ति वेदान्तः पुराणं परमन्त्विदं //
382.m: There can be no established doctrine higher than this; there is no highest auspiciousness [apart from it]. / There is no Vedānta higher than this; this Purāṇa is indeed supreme.

382.s:
nāsmātparataraṃ bhūmau vidyate vastu durlabham /
āgneye hi purāṇe 'smin sarvavidyāḥ pradarśitāḥ //
382.d:
नास्मात्परतरं भूमौ विद्यते वस्तु दुर्लभम् /
आग्नेये हि पुराणे ऽस्मिन् सर्वविद्याः प्रदर्शिताः //
382.m: There exists on earth no rare object higher than this. / For in this Agni Purāṇa, all sciences have been shown.

382.s:
sarve matsyāvatārādyā gītā rāmāyaṇantviha /
harivaṃśo bhāratañca nava sargāḥ pradarśitāḥ //
382.d:
सर्वे मत्स्यावताराद्या गीता रामायणन्त्विह /
हरिवंशो भारतञ्च नव सर्गाः प्रदर्शिताः //
382.m: All [incarnations] beginning with the fish incarnation have been sung, and here the Rāmāyaṇa, / the Harivaṃśa and the Mahābhārata, and the nine creations have been shown.

382.s:
āgamo vaiṣṇavo gītaḥ pūjādīkṣāpratiṣṭhayā /
pavitrārohaṇādīni pratimālakṣaṇādikaṃ //
382.d:
आगमो वैष्णवो गीतः पूजादीक्षाप्रतिष्ठया /
पवित्रारोहणादीनि प्रतिमालक्षणादिकं //
382.m: The Vaiṣṇava Āgama has been sung, with worship, initiation, and consecration, / rites such as investiture with the sacred thread, and the characteristics of images and the like,

382.s:
prāsādalakṣaṇādyañca mantrā vai bhuktimuktidāḥ /
śaivāgamastadarthaś ca śākteyaḥ saura eva ca //
382.d:
प्रासादलक्षणाद्यञ्च मन्त्रा वै भुक्तिमुक्तिदाः /
शैवागमस्तदर्थश् च शाक्तेयः सौर एव च //
382.m: the characteristics of temples and so forth, and the mantras that bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation; / the Śaiva Āgama and its meaning, as well as the Śākta and the Saura [traditions],

382.s:
maṇḍalāni ca vāstuś ca mantāṇi vividhāni ca /
pratisargaścānugīto brahmāṇḍaparimaṇḍalaṃ //
:p 359
382.d:
मण्डलानि च वास्तुश् च मन्ताणि विविधानि च /
प्रतिसर्गश्चानुगीतो ब्रह्माण्डपरिमण्डलं //
:प् 359
382.m:
the maṇḍalas, site architecture, various mantras, / and secondary creation have been sung, [as well as] the circumference of the cosmic egg.
[p. 359]

382.s:
gīto bhuvanakoṣaś ca dvīpavarṣādinimnagāḥ /
gayāgaṅgāprayāgādi tīrthamāhātmyamīritaṃ //
382.d:
गीतो भुवनकोषश् च द्वीपवर्षादिनिम्नगाः /
गयागङ्गाप्रयागादि तीर्थमाहात्म्यमीरितं //
382.m: The description of the earth has been sung, the continents, regions, and rivers; / the greatness of sacred fords such as Gayā, the Gaṅgā, and Prayāga has been declared;

382.s:
jyotiś cakraṃ jyotiṣādi gīto yuddhajayārṇavaḥ /
manvantarādayo gītāḥ dharmā varṇādikasya ca //
382.d:
ज्योतिश् चक्रं ज्योतिषादि गीतो युद्धजयार्णवः /
मन्वन्तरादयो गीताः धर्मा वर्णादिकस्य च //
382.m: the wheel of the heavenly bodies, astrology and astronomy, and the Yuddhajayārṇava have been sung; / the cosmic eras of Manus and the rest have been sung, and the duties of the castes and life-stages;

382.s:
aśaucaṃ dravyaśuddhiś ca prāyaścittaṃ pradarśitaṃ /
rājadharmā dānadharmā vratāni vividhāni ca //
382.d:
अशौचं द्रव्यशुद्धिश् च प्रायश्चित्तं प्रदर्शितं /
राजधर्मा दानधर्मा व्रतानि विविधानि च //
382.m: ritual impurity, purification of substances, and expiation have been shown; / the duties of kings, the duties regarding gifts, and various votive observances;

382.s:
vyavahārāḥ śāntayaś ca ṛgvedādividhānakaṃ /
sūryavaṃśaḥ somavaṃśo dhanurvedaś ca vaidyakaṃ //
382.d:
व्यवहाराः शान्तयश् च ऋग्वेदादिविधानकं /
सूर्यवंशः सोमवंशो धनुर्वेदश् च वैद्यकं //
382.m: legal procedures, propitiatory rites, and the ritual applications of the Ṛgveda and other [Vedas]; / the Solar dynasty, the Lunar dynasty, the science of archery, and medicine;

382.s:
gāndharvavedo 'rthaśāstraṃ mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ /
purāṇasaṃkhyāmāhatmyaṃ chando vyakaraṇaṃ smṛtaṃ //
382.d:
गान्धर्ववेदो ऽर्थशास्त्रं मीमांसा न्यायविस्तरः /
पुराणसंख्यामाहत्म्यं छन्दो व्यकरणं स्मृतं //
382.m: the science of music, statecraft, Mīmāṃsā, extensive Nyāya, / the count and greatness of the Purāṇas, metrics, and grammar are taught;

382.s:
alaṅkāro vighaṇḍuś ca śikṣākalpa ihoditaḥ smṛtaḥ /
naimittikaḥ prākṛtiko laya ātyantikaḥ //
382.d:
अलङ्कारो विघण्डुश् च शिक्षाकल्प इहोदितः स्मृतः /
नैमित्तिकः प्राकृतिको लय आत्यन्तिकः //
382.m: poetics, lexicography, phonetics, and ritual procedures are declared and taught here; / incidental dissolution, elemental dissolution, and final dissolution;

382.s:
vedāntaṃ brahmavijñānaṃ yogo hy aṣṭāṅga īritaḥ /
stotraṃ purāṇamāhātmyaṃ vidyā hy aṣṭādaśa smṛtāḥ //
382.d:
वेदान्तं ब्रह्मविज्ञानं योगो ह्य् अष्टाङ्ग ईरितः /
स्तोत्रं पुराणमाहात्म्यं विद्या ह्य् अष्टादश स्मृताः //
382.m: Vedānta, the realization of Brahman, and eight-limbed yoga have been taught; / hymns of praise, the greatness of the Purāṇa, and the eighteen sciences are commemorated;

382.s:
ṛgvedādyāḥ parā hy atra parāvidyākṣaraṃ paraṃ /
saprapañcaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ brahmaṇo rūpamīritaṃ //
382.d:
ऋग्वेदाद्याः परा ह्य् अत्र पराविद्याक्षरं परं /
सप्रपञ्चं निष्प्रपञ्चं ब्रह्मणो रूपमीरितं //
382.m: the [sciences] beginning with the Ṛgveda are lower here, while the higher knowledge is the supreme Imperishable. / The form of Brahman has been declared, both differentiated and undifferentiated.

382.s:
idaṃ pañcadaśasohasraṃ śatakoṭipravistaraṃ /
devaloke daivataiś ca purāṇaṃ paṭhyate sadā //
382.d:
इदं पञ्चदशसोहस्रं शतकोटिप्रविस्तरं /
देवलोके दैवतैश् च पुराणं पठ्यते सदा //
382.m: Consisting of fifteen thousand [verses], this Purāṇa extending to a hundred crores [of verses] / is constantly recited by the deities in the celestial realm.

382.s:
lokānāṃ hitakāmena saṃkṣipyodgītamagninā /
sarvaṃ brahmeti jānīdhvaṃ munayaḥ śaunakādayaḥ //
382.d:
लोकानां हितकामेन संक्षिप्योद्गीतमग्निना /
सर्वं ब्रह्मेति जानीध्वं मुनयः शौनकादयः //
382.m: Out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds, it was sung in an abridged form by Agni. / Know that everything is Brahman, O sages headed by Śaunaka!

382.s:
śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi yaḥ paṭhetpāṭhayedapi /
likhellekhāpayedvāpi yujayetkīrtayedapi //
382.d:
शृणुयाच्छ्रावयेद्वापि यः पठेत्पाठयेदपि /
लिखेल्लेखापयेद्वापि युजयेत्कीर्तयेदपि //
382.m: Whoever hears it or causes it to be heard, recites it or causes it to be recited, / writes it or causes it to be written, practices it or praises it—

382.s:
purāṇapāṭhakañcaiva pūjayet prayato nṛpaḥ /
:p 360
gobhūhiraṇyadānādyair vastrālaṅkāratarpaṇaiḥ //
382.d:
पुराणपाठकञ्चैव पूजयेत् प्रयतो नृपः /
:प् 360
गोभूहिरण्यदानाद्यैर् वस्त्रालङ्कारतर्पणैः //
382.m:
and a king, restrained in mind, should worship the reciter of the Purāṇa,
[p. 360]
with gifts of cows, land, gold, and other [offerings], with garments, ornaments, and gratifications.

382.s:
taṃ saṃpūjya labheccaiva purāṇaśravaṇāt phalaṃ /
purāṇānte ca vai kuryādavaśyaṃ dvijabhojanaṃ //
382.d:
तं संपूज्य लभेच्चैव पुराणश्रवणात् फलं /
पुराणान्ते च वै कुर्यादवश्यं द्विजभोजनं //
382.m: Having honoured him, one indeed obtains the fruit from hearing the Purāṇa. / And at the conclusion of the Purāṇa, one must necessarily feed twice-born [Brahmins].

382.s:
nirmalaḥ prāptasarvārthaḥ sakulaḥ svargamāpnuyāt /
śarayantraṃ pustakāya sūtraṃ vai patrasañcayaṃ //
382.d:
निर्मलः प्राप्तसर्वार्थः सकुलः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् /
शरयन्त्रं पुस्तकाय सूत्रं वै पत्रसञ्चयं //
382.m: Pure, having achieved all purposes, he would reach heaven together with his family. / A reading-stand for the manuscript, thread, a bundle of leaves,

382.s:
paṭṭikābandhavastrādi dadyād yaḥ svargamāpnuyāt /
yo dadyādbrahmalokī syāt pustakaṃ yasya vai gṛhe //
382.d:
पट्टिकाबन्धवस्त्रादि दद्याद् यः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् /
यो दद्याद्ब्रह्मलोकी स्यात् पुस्तकं यस्य वै गृहे //
382.m: cloth for binding, wooden covers, and so forth: whoever gives these reaches heaven. / He who gives [a copy] becomes an inhabitant of the realm of Brahmā. Indeed, in whosever house the book [abides],

382.s:
tasyotpātabhayaṃ nāsti bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
yūyaṃ samarata cāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ rūpamaiśvaraṃ /
sūto gataḥ pujitastaiḥ śaunakādyā hariṃ yāyaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe āgneyapurāṇamāhātmyaṃ nāma
dvyaśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
samāptamāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ
:p 361
athāgnipurāṇa pariśiṣṭam
382.d:
तस्योत्पातभयं नास्ति भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् /
यूयं समरत चाग्नेयं पुराणं रूपमैश्वरं /
सूतो गतः पुजितस्तैः शौनकाद्या हरिं यायः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे आग्नेयपुराणमाहात्म्यं नाम
द्व्यशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
समाप्तमाग्नेयं पुराणं
:प् 361
अथाग्निपुराण परिशिष्टम्
382.m:
he has no fear of portents, and attains worldly enjoyment and liberation. / May you constantly remember the Agni Purāṇa, the divine form! / Honoured by them, Sūta departed, and Śaunaka and the others went to Hari.
Thus ends the three hundred and eighty-second chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled “The Greatness of the Agni Purāṇa.”
The Agni Purāṇa is complete. / [p. 361]
Now begins the appendix to the Agni Purāṇa.

382.s:
agnipurāṇasya kakārādi-cihnita-daśasaṃkhyakādarśa-pustakānāṃ
madhye navasu ādarśapustakeṣu yamagītādhyāyāt paraṃ
purāṇa-māhātmyādhyāyena pustakaṃ sampūrṇaṃ / ga-cihnita-pustake
tu yama-gītādhyāyāt paraṃ atiriktatrayastriṃśat
saṃkhyakasṛṣṭiprakaraṇādyadhyāyā vartante / uktādhyāyānāṃ
navasu ādarśapustakeṣu avidyamānatvāt pramāṇyaṃ sandigdhaṃ /
prāmāṇyepi sthānaviśeṣe

Among the ten exemplar manuscripts of the Agni Purāṇa marked with ‘ka’ and subsequent letters, in nine exemplar manuscripts the text concludes with the chapter on the greatness of the Purāṇa following the Yamagītā chapter. In the manuscript marked ‘ga’, however, following the Yamagītā chapter, there are thirty-three additional chapters beginning with the section on creation. Because these said chapters are absent in nine exemplar manuscripts, their authenticity is doubtful. Even granting authenticity, since only one manuscript, that marked ‘ga’, is available—which is defective with missing letters in various places—I was unable to print these additional chapters here. Nevertheless, for the purpose of making this known, a few additional chapters found only in the manuscript marked ‘ga’ have been emended to the best of my ability and printed in the form of an appendix. Because the manuscript marked ‘ga’ has missing letters and is corrupt, faulty readings exist in many places of this appendix.

Six of those months make an ayana; there are two ayanas: southern and northern.
The southern ayana is night for the gods, and the northern is day.
Two ayanas are declared to be a year for mortals;
a month of human beings is taught to be a day and night for the ancestors.
A human year is traditionally held to be a day and night for the Vasus and other gods.
Hear from me the division of those [ages] designated as Kṛta, Tretā, and so on,
by thousands of divine years: four, [three, two, and one], into twelve.
Four, three, two, and one, respectively, in the Kṛta and following [yugas],
thousands of divine years in the yugas, the knowers of the past say.
Measured by that many hundreds, the dawn preceding each is named there.
And the twilight following it is equal to that; it indeed comes after the yuga.
The period of time that exists between dawn and twilight, O twice-born,
is to be known as a yuga, designated as Kṛta, Tretā, and so on.

Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali: this is the four-yuga cycle.
A thousand of them is called a day of Brahmā, O twice-born.
[page 363]
In a day of Brahmā, O sage, there are fourteen Manus.
Their auspicious measurement made by time is [as follows]:
the Seven Sages, the gods, Śakra, the Manu, and his sons, the kings,
are created at one time and destroyed as before.
Seventy-one cycles of four yugas are enumerated
as a manvantara, the time of a Manu, and of Śakra and the others as well, O twice-born.
Eight hundred and fifty-two thousand by divine count, [O Sūta,]
and fifty-one other [years], and seven others, O sage,
and twenty thousand—this time is traditionally stated with an excess.
Thus should a day of Brahmā be known; it is proclaimed as this.

382.m:
Thus ends the first chapter, named the Section on Creation, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the second chapter.
Sūta said:
Here, while the god was asleep, a lotus arose from his navel.
In that lotus, O fortunate one, he who is versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
Brahmā was born; he was addressed by him: "Create creatures, O high-minded one!"
Having spoken thus, the lord Nārāyaṇa vanished.
Thinking of the god Viṣṇu, who had gone after saying, "So be it,"
Brahmā remained; he did not comprehend at all any cause for the universe.
Then great anger arose in that great-souled Brahmā.
From that, Rudra was born upon his lap, originating from his wrath.
Crying, he was addressed by that Brahmā of unmanifest birth:
When told, "Give me a name," he gave him [the name] Rudra.
He too was told by him: "Create this world again!"

382.m:
Endowed with ascetic austerity, he repeatedly created in the exhausted waters.
[Page 365]
When he was immersed in the waters, however, another Prajāpati
Brahmā, the lord of beings, created standing to his right, and another
Dakṣa, who stood to his left, and then he brought forth his wife.
With her he engendered the lord Manu Svāyambhuva.
From him the creation of living beings was effected thus by Brahmā.
In this way the creation has been related by me to you, O best of sages,
of the Lord of the universe as he created. What further do you wish to hear?
Bharadvāja said:
"This has been narrated in brief by you to me, O Lomaharṣaṇa.
Speak again in detail of the primary creation, O high-minded one!"
Sūta said:
"At the end of this cosmic egg, the lord awakened from night-sleep;
then Brahmā, filled with the quality of sattva, looked upon the empty world.

382.m:
Nārāyaṇa is to be worshipped by the highest, the first-born even of the ancients,
the blessed one whose nature is Brahman, beginningless, the source of all.
[…] this verse regarding Nārāyaṇa,
the god whose form is Brahman, the imperishable source of the world:
'The waters are called nārāḥ; the waters are indeed the offspring of Nara.
That was his primary resting place (ayana); therefore he is called Nārāyaṇa.'
As he was contemplating creation, as previously at the beginnings of the kalpas,
there arose for him, devoid of growth, [a creation] full of delusion:
darkness (tamas), delusion (moha), great delusion (mahāmoha), and that named blinding darkness (tāmisra and andhatāmisra)—
five kinds of ignorance arose of that great-souled one before all else.

382.m:
Again, as he was meditating upon another, superior creation,
the transverse stream (tiryak-śrotas) arose; […] it is recorded as the transverse stream.
They are well known as animals and the like; they follow the wrong path.
Thinking that creation of the transverse stream to be incapable of fulfilling the purpose, the four-faced one [meditated again].
The third [creation], the upward stream (ūrdhva-śrotas), moved above the earthly realm.
From that arose the gods who move upward, born along with the creation.
When the Prajāpati was not satisfied with that creation, then he paused,
considering those born from the primary creation to be ineffective.
Then as he was reflecting, O brāhmaṇa, that [creation] is remembered as the downward stream (arvāk-śrotas).
Human beings, born thus as the downward stream, are considered capable of achieving the purpose.
They possess illumination, but are born with darkness and have an excess of rajas;
therefore they endure sorrow and are continually active.
Thus these creations have been recounted to you, O best of sages.

382.m:
The first is the creation of Mahat; the second is that of the subtle elements (tanmātras).
The third is the transformational (vaikārika) creation, known as that of the sense organs.
The fourth is the primary creation (mukhya-sarga); […] the immovables are recorded.
The fifth is that called the transverse stream (tiryak-śrotas), the animal species.
Then the sixth is that of the upward streams; the seventh is the creation of the gods.
Then the best, of the downward stream, is the seventh [or eighth], the human creation.
The eighth is the supportive creation (anugraha-sarga); it is both sāttvika and tāmasa."
The ninth is the creation of Rudra. These are the nine creations of Prajāpati.
[Page 367]
These five are secondary creations; the primary creations are traditionally remembered, O dear one.
Both the primary and the secondary creations are the root causes of the world.
They are the creation arising from Brahmā as he creates, which have been related by me.
Then, entering with his potency, the supreme modification, he created everything—

Now begins the third chapter.
The Topic of Creation
Bharadvāja said:
The ninefold creation arose from Brahmā, who is born of the Unmanifest.
How did it multiply, O Sūta? Tell me this now.
Sūta said:
First created by Brahmā, following Rudra, were those rich in ascetic austerity:
Sanaka and the others, who were created, as well as Marīci and the others:
Marīci, Atri, and likewise Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu,
and Pulastya of great splendour, Pracetas, and Bhṛgu,
and Nārada as the tenth, and Vasiṣṭha of great brilliance.
Sanaka and the others were established in the duty called cessation;
[Page 368]
Marīci and the others in the duty called engagement; the sage Nārada solely in liberation.

through the lineage of his daughters' sons, this entire universe of moving and unmoving beings,
the gods, the Dānavas, the Gandharvas, serpents, and birds,
all supremely righteous, were born of Dakṣa’s daughters.
The four classes of beings, both unmoving and moving,
multiplied, and so did those originating from the creation of the Manus.
The great sages, Marīci and the others, were the makers of the creation of the Manus,
as were the highly fortunate Vasiṣṭha and the others, born from the mind of Brahmā.
In these creations, that Supreme Self creates beings, beginning with the ether, through Time;

How did Vasiṣṭha become the son of Mitra and Varuṇa,
having previously been born from the mind of Brahmā, O one of great destiny?
Sūta said:
I shall declare the creation of Rudra and his production, O good one;
and hear in detail as I declare the secondary creation of the sages.
At the beginning of the kalpa, as he was meditating upon a son equal to himself,
there appeared from the body of the Lord a youth of blue and red colour,
having the form of the Lord who is half-female, fierce, with an immense body,
illuminating all the cardinal and intermediate directions with his splendour.
Seeing him blazing with splendour, Prajāpati replied:
"Divide yourself today at my command, O highly intelligent one!"
Being thus addressed by Brahmā, the glorious Rudra there
then separated his female nature and his male nature.

He divided the male nature into eleven parts.
I will tell you their names; hear them from me, O best of the twice-born:
Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Kapālin, and Rudra,
Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka, and Aparājita,
Vṛṣākapi, Śambhu, Kapardin, and likewise Raivata—
these are declared to be the eleven Rudras, lords of the three worlds.
And in the same way Rudra divided femininity tenfold and singly;
she remained standing as his wife in manifold forms.
When formerly he performed terrifying ascetic austerity lying on his back in the water,
then that lord, the mighty Rudra, created there,
by the power of ascetic austerity, O best of Brahmins, various beings:
[Page 370]

and Svāhā is to be known as the tenth, and Svadhā is recorded as the eleventh.
And these were given by Dakṣa to the purified sages.
And those who were the sons of Marīci and the others, them I tell unto you:
Marīci's wife Sambhūti gave birth to the sage Kaśyapa.

besought by the gods headed by Brahmā, took an incarnation here.
Kardama, Ambarīṣa, and Sahiṣṇu—a triad of sons
Kṣamā, the wife of Pulastya Prajāpati, bore.
[Page 372]
And Kratu's wife Satvatī gave birth to the Vālakhilyas,
those sixty thousand sages of vital fluid drawn upward,
of the size of a thumb-joint, blazing with the splendour of the sun.
Then from Pracetas, in Satyā, three sons of true resolve
were born; and their sons and grandsons were hundreds and thousands.
And in Ūrjā seven sons were born to Vasiṣṭha:
Rajas, Ūrdhvabāhu, Śaraṇa, and Anagha […]
Surūpa, and Śukra—these all became the seven sages.
From Bhṛgu and Khyāti was born Lakṣmī, the wife of Viṣṇu.

Likewise, Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ were born as two sons of Bhṛgu through Khyāti.
Āyati and Niyati were the very lovely daughters of Meru;
they were the wives of Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ. From the two [couples] were born two sons:
Prāṇa and Mṛkaṇḍu; Mārkaṇḍeya was the son of Mṛkaṇḍu,
by whom death was conquered long ago, O Brahmin, through Nārāyaṇa.
From him Devaśiras was born; Prāṇa also had a son
renowned as Dyutimān; Sañjaya was his son.
From them, O fortunate one, the lineage of Bhṛgu attained wide expansion.
And he who was named Agni, the eldest son of Brahmā,
from him Svāhā bore three sons of noble energy, O twice-born ones:
Pāvaka, Pavamāna, and Śuci who consumes water.

these are spoken of in many ways, along with the father and the three grandsons;
thus, through their lineage, forty-nine are proclaimed.
The ancestors created by Brahmā, whom I have explained to you,
from them Svadhā bore two daughters: Menā and Dhāriṇī.
Dakṣa, who had formerly been commanded by the Self-born to create offspring:
hear from me, O best of men, how he created living beings.
Formerly Dakṣa created beings by his mind, O sage:
gods, sages, along with Gandharvas, Asuras, and serpents.
When, as he created, creatures did not multiply,
then the sage, the lord of creatures, reflected for the sake of creation.
Desiring to create various creatures by sexual reproduction,
[he took] Asiknī, the daughter of the lord of creatures Vīraṇa.
Dakṣa created sixty daughters upon Vīriṇī—so runs our tradition;

twenty-seven to Soma, four to Ariṣṭanemi,
two to Bahuputra, and two to Aṅgiras,
and two to the wise Kṛśāśva; hear from me their offspring.
Viśvā bore the Viśvedevas, and Sādhyā bore the Sādhyas;
the Maruts were born of Marutvatī, and the Vasus are traditionally considered [born] of Vasu.
The Bhānu gods were born of Bhānu, and the Muhūrtajas were born of Muhūrtā;
Ghoṣa was born of Lambā, and the Jāmijas were born of Jāmī;

Their sons and grandsons were hundreds and thousands;

Aditi, Diti, Danu, Ariṣṭā, Surasā,
Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhā, Khasā, Irā,
Kadrū, and Muni, O knower of righteousness—hear from me their offspring.
Twelve splendid sons were born to Kaśyapa by Aditi;
I shall state them by name, hear as I speak:
Bhaga, Aṃśa, Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa,
Savitṛ, Dhātṛ, and Vivasvat, O noble-minded one,
Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan, Indra likewise, and Viṣṇu is said to be the twelfth.
Two sons were born to Kaśyapa by Diti, so we have heard:
the immense-bodied Hiraṇyākṣa, who was slain by the Boar,

and many other powerful Daityas, sons of Diti.
From Ariṣṭā the Gandharvas were born […],
and from Surasā arose many hosts of Vidyādharas.
The sage Kaśyapa begot cattle upon Surabhi.
From Vinatā, however, two sons were born, renowned as Garuḍa and Aruṇa.
[page 375]
Garuḍa, out of affection, became the mount of Viṣṇu,
the God of gods of boundless splendor; and Aruṇa became the charioteer of the Sun.
Six sons were born from Tāmrā by Kaśyapa; learn of them from me:
horses, camels, donkeys, elephants, gavayas, and deer.
Likewise, in Krodhā were born beasts of vicious species;
Irā [bore] the species of trees, creeping plants, vines, grasses, and horses as offspring.
Khasā, however, [bore] the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas; Muni [bore] the Apsarases;
and Kadru's sons were the great serpents, biting snakes of ferocious venom.

382.m:
Those who are proclaimed as the twenty-seven wives of Soma, devoted to sacred vows—
their sons, O twice-born one, were beings of great strength, beginning with Budha.
Sixteen were the offspring of the wives of Ariṣṭanemi here.
Of the wise Bahuputra, lightning and others were born in Tāmrā.
The sons of Pratyaṅgiras were the foremost sages honored by sages;
and the divine sage Kṛśāśva's sons were the divine weapons.
These indeed are born again at the end of a thousand yugas.
These are proclaimed as the descendants of Kaśyapa, stationary and moving.
Through their sons, grandsons, and descendants, the creation of Prajāpati multiplied,
for the god Nārasiṃha the wise, who is firmly established.
These manifestations, O brāhmaṇa, have been proclaimed to you by me.
The progeny of the daughters of Dakṣa has been narrated to you by me.
Whoever, endowed with faith, remembers these, will obtain fame and lineage.

382.m:
Primary creation and secondary creation have been spoken to you by me in brief, for the purpose of the expansion of creation.
[page 376]
Those men who, devoted to Viṣṇu, always recite this, O twice-born ones,
become spotless.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Section on Creation," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now the fifth chapter:
The account of Vasiṣṭha being the son of Mitra and Varuṇa.
Sūta said:
The creation of the world by Viṣṇu, the Great-souled, has been told to you by me, O twice-born one,
as well as how gods, Dānavas, Yakṣas, and others were brought forth.
Regarding that which was asked of me by you previously in the presence of the sages—
namely, how Vasiṣṭha came to be the son of Mitra and Varuṇa—
that sacred ancient narrative I shall tell.
Listen with an attentive mind, O Bharadvāja, to what is uttered by me.
A knower of the truth of all duty and purpose, the best of all who know,
one who has reached the further shore of all branches of knowledge, was the Prajāpati named Dakṣa.

382.m:
By him thirteen auspicious daughters were given to Kaśyapa.
I shall speak their names; learn them from me now:
Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kāṣṭhā, Muhūrtā, Siṃhikā, O sage,
Srutā, Kroṣṭā, Surabhi, Vinatā, Surasā, […]
Kadru, Surasā, and also Yātudevī remembered as Śunī—
these were the daughters of Dakṣa; he gave them to Kaśyapa.
[page 377]
The eldest and most eminent among them was named Aditi.
Aditi gave birth to twelve sons possessing brilliance equal to fire.
I shall speak their names; listen, O best of the twice-born,
by whom this daytime and night constantly proceeds in succession:
Bharga, Aṃśu, Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa,
Savitṛ, Dhātṛ, and Vivasvat, O one of great intellect,
Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan, then Indra, and Viṣṇu is remembered as the twelfth.

Her middle son was named Varuṇa;
known as a World Protector, he is proclaimed in the western quarter.
In the western quarter of the western ocean shines
the glorious mountain named Asta, made of gold,
with peaks made of all manner of gems, accompanied by mineral cascades.
Endowed [with them], that mountain shines, composed of various jewels and auspicious,
with deep caves and resounding with lions and tigers,
frequented by gods and Gandharvas in various secluded regions.
When the sun has set behind it, the world is filled with darkness.
Upon its peak is a most divine, auspicious [city] made of gold,
delightful, constructed by Viśvakarman with jeweled pillars,
a city named Sukhāvatī, abundant with means of enjoyment.

his body radiant with celestial scents, adorned with divine ornaments,

endowed with various flowers and fruits, filled with various […]

Seeing that form of the slender woman, the two gods were overcome by passion.
By her laughter, dance, smile, and charm,
by the soft, cool, and fragrant [breeze],
by the humming of intoxicated bees and the call of male cuckoos,
and indeed by Urvaśī's melodious and sweet singing,
and looked upon with a side-glance, both of them discharged their semen.
“Vasiṣṭha, you are the son of Mitra and Varuṇa,” the Viśvedevas having arrived there said;
the semen divided into parts in the lotus, […].
That semen fell in three parts: into a lotus, onto the dry ground, and into the water.
In the lotus, Vasiṣṭha was born, O best of sages;
on the dry ground Agastya was born, and in the water the Matsya of great luster.

Having attained his desire through ascetic austerity, [he reached] the supreme, eternal light.
As the two foremost of gods were practicing ascetic austerity, Brahmā approached and said:
“O gods Mitra and Varuṇa, endowed with sons, of great splendor,
may there be supreme Vaiṣṇava perfection for both of you again.
Now, remain in your own sphere of authority as witnesses of the world.”
Having spoken thus, Brahmā vanished, and the two remained in their own offices.
Thus has been recounted to you, O Brahmin, the great-souled Vasiṣṭha's
and the wise Agastya's being sons of Mitra and Varuṇa.
This ancient narrative that bestows male progeny destroys sins.
Having heard it, a king together with his ministers and sons is freed from sin.

382.m:
And whatever people, observing pure vows, hear this desiring sons,
they obtain sons without delay; there is no doubt in this.
And whoever constantly recites this during offerings to gods and ancestors, O best of the twice-born,
his gods and ancestors depart satisfied as they please.
And that human being who recites this daily upon rising in the morning
obtains very great sons and goes to the heavenly world.
The excellent [narrative] spoken of old by those devoted to the Veda has been recounted by me.
Whoever will recite or always hears it,
he, purified, swiftly goes to the superior realm.
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the glorious Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Account of Vasiṣṭha’s Being the Son of Mitra and Varuṇa'.

382.m:
Listen from me to this great narrative, O Bharadvāja;
let all the sages listen, I tell what occurred in the past:
In the immensely sacred Kurukṣetra, at the seat of Vyāsa in the excellent hermitage,
the best of sages, the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, was seated there,
having bathed and performed his recitation, surrounded by sage-disciples,
knower of the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, expert in all scriptures.
Having bowed down properly, the exceedingly righteous Śuka,
referring to this very matter, asked him with folded hands
concerning the very matter about which we have been questioned here by you in the presence of the sages,
by you, a devotee of Narasiṃha and dweller at the sacred ford.
Śuka said:
How was death defeated by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya?
Tell this to me, father; I wish to hear it from you now.

From Bhṛgu, through Khyāti, a son named Mṛkaṇḍu was indeed born,
and of the great-souled Mṛkaṇḍu, there was a wife named Sumitrā,
knower of dharma, devoted to dharma, intent on service to her husband.
To him, upon her, was born the son Mārkaṇḍeya of great intellect,
the grandson of Bhṛgu, highly fortunate, […] of great intellect.
The beloved boy grew up, his father having performed the rites for him there.
Indeed, as soon as he was born, an astrologer stated:
'In his twelfth year, the son will be afflicted by death.'
Hearing that, his mother and father both became grief-stricken,
their hearts overcome with sorrow as they gazed upon that highly intelligent one.

recounted all that which the astrologer had said.
Having heard that, he, very resolute, spoke again to his mother and father:
“O mother, together with my father, not even the slightest grief should be felt by you.
I will avert death […] by ascetic austerity; there is no doubt of this.
And I will perform great ascetic austerity so that I attain a long lifespan.”
Having said this, comforting his parents […],
he went to the forest filled with various sages.
There he saw his grandfather comfortably seated together with the sages,
the righteous Bhṛgu, [saw] the highly intelligent Mārkaṇḍeya.
Then Bhṛgu said to the fortunate child Mārkaṇḍeya:
“Why have you come, my son? Is it well with your father,
with your mother, and with your relatives? What is the reason for your coming?”

382.m:
Being thus addressed by the great-souled sage,
Mārkaṇḍeya then told him all the words of the astrologer.
Having heard the words of his grandson, Bhṛgu spoke to him again:
“Such is your thought, O one of great intellect! What action do you wish to perform?”
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
“I desire now to conquer death, which snatches away living beings.

Through your instruction, O Guru, tell us the means for that.”
The Guru said:
“Without having worshipped Nārāyaṇa with the mind through ascetic austerity, O son,
who could conquer death? Therefore worship him with ascetic austerity!
Him, the [unborn] Viṣṇu, Acyuta, Puruṣottama,
who loves his devotees, the highest of the gods—go to him for refuge with devotion!
The sage Nārada formerly went to him alone for refuge
through great ascetic austerity, O child—to the sorrowless Nārāyaṇa.

382.m:
By his grace, O fortunate one, Nārada, the son of Brahmā,
having conquered old age and death, lives happily with a long life.
Who except that lotus-eyed Nārasiṃha, Janārdana,
affectionate toward his devotees, could ward off the army of death?
Therefore, constantly take refuge in Viṣṇu, the creator of the world, the victorious lord of Śrī,
Govinda, the lord of cattle, the god!
If you always worship the unborn god Nārasiṃha,
O child, you will conquer death together with his army; there is no doubt of this.”
Vyāsa said:
Being thus addressed by his grandfather Bhṛgu,
Mārkaṇḍeya of great splendour then spoke with humility to his grandfather:
“O father, you have spoken with certainty that only Viṣṇu is to be worshipped,
and that the Blessed Lord, when worshipped, will take away my death.
How, in this matter, should the worship of Acyuta be performed by me, O Guru,
